question: Should this repository intentionally disable previously runnable Droid, Copilot, and OpenCode autoreviews to enforce the canonical isolation boundary?
rationale: Failing closed is the safest implementation, but it breaks existing engine-selected workflows; choosing hard removal, an explicit unsafe compatibility mode, or deferral requires repository-owner intent.

options.title: Approve fail-closed removal
options.body: Accept the break, correct the compatibility statement, and document Codex, Claude, or Pi as the supported migration path.

options.title: Add unsafe opt-in
options.body: Retain legacy engines only behind a conspicuous default-off switch that states their missing repository, filesystem, and network isolation guarantees.

options.title: Defer the sync
options.body: Wait until those reviewer CLIs expose adequate isolation or the canonical project adopts another compatibility policy.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed removal
recommendation.body: Accept the break, correct the compatibility statement, and document Codex, Claude, or Pi as the supported migration path.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc introduced the feature and authored the canonical hardening and downstream sync, providing the strongest evidence of intended security behavior.
